player.q: How do I find a drill or skill move?
player.intro: There are two ways in, depending on whether you know the name of the move.

steps.text: If you know the move by name — Maradona, elastico, roulette — use Search Key Skill Moves and type it in.
If you are browsing, open All Programs and pick a skill area on the left, then a sub-category.
Open the folder to see the videos inside it. Each folder runs easiest to hardest, so start at the top.

player.q: How do I mark a video as done?
player.intro: Your progress, points and streak all come from videos you have marked done — so do this every session.

steps.text: Open the video and train along with it.
When you finish, tap the Mark as Done / complete button under the player.
The video gets a green check and the minutes are added to your training time.
If you marked one by mistake, tap it again to undo it.

player.q: How do I get a training plan?
player.intro: A plan tells you what to train each week so you are not choosing from scratch every day.

steps.text: Go to Get a Training Plan.
Pick the plan type — Skill Builder if you are not sure — then choose the skill areas you want to work on.
Choose how many weeks you want to run it for and confirm.
Your plan then shows up under Training Plans, and that is where you train from each day.

player.q: How does my weekly plan work?
player.intro: Every plan works the same way: a weekly goal plus a day pointer that you move yourself.

steps.text: Each week has a target — a number of videos and an amount of training time.
Train the videos shown for the day you are on.
Tap Mark done to move to the next day. Nothing moves on automatically, so you can never fall behind.
When the last day is done, the plan is complete and you can build a new one.

player.q: How do I save videos I want to come back to?
player.intro: Favorites are your own shortlist — folders and videos you want on hand.

steps.text: Tap the star / heart on any video or folder to pin it.
Everything you pin collects under My Favorites.
Tap the star again to unpin it.

player.q: How do I join a team?
player.intro: Your coach starts the team — you join it, you do not create it.

steps.text: Ask your coach for the team join link or code.
Open the link and confirm the player you are joining as.
The team then shows under My Teams.
If the link does not work, check with your coach that your spot on the team is still open.

player.q: Where do I find my homework?
player.intro: Homework is what your coach has assigned to you specifically.

steps.text: Open Homework from the menu.
Work through the folders your coach assigned — anything with a due date is shown first.
Mark each video done as you go. Your coach sees your progress on their board.

player.intro: The leaderboard ranks players on what they have actually trained.

steps.text: You earn your place by completing videos and logging training time — marking videos done is what counts.
Open the Leaderboard to see where you sit.
Use the tabs to switch between boards — overall, streaks, levels and team boards.
Rankings refresh regularly, so train today and check back.

player.intro: Badges are awarded automatically for hitting milestones — you do not have to claim them.

steps.text: Keep completing videos and logging training time.
When you cross a milestone the badge is added to your collection.
See everything you have earned under My Badges.

player.intro: The passport turns your training into a trip around the world.

steps.text: Every block of videos you complete earns you a stamp.
Each stamp moves you on to the next country.
Open Travel Passport to see your stamps and where you are headed next.

player.q: Where can I see my progress?
player.intro: Goals & Reports is the full picture — time trained, videos done and how you are trending.

steps.text: Open Goals & Reports.
Set a weekly goal so the reports have something to measure you against.
Check back weekly — the trend matters more than any single day.

player.q: How do I add a highlight clip?
player.intro: Player Highlights is where your own clips live, separate from the training videos.

steps.text: Open Player Highlights.
Tap to upload and choose the clip from your phone or computer.
Give it a title so people know what they are watching, then save.

player.intro: Your profile is what coaches and other players see.

steps.text: Open My Public Profile from the menu — it shows your badges, level and training totals.
Keep training to fill it out; everything on it is earned, not entered.

player.intro: Yes — the Learning Center has short videos covering the same ground as this guide.

steps.text: Open the Learning Center.
Start with How to Get Started, then How to Use the All Programs Area.

player.q: Something is not working — who do I ask?
player.intro: Try these in order before anything else.

steps.text: Pull down to refresh, or close the app and open it again.
If a video will not play, check you are on a good connection — the player drops quality on weak signal.
If it is about your team, your homework or your spot on a team, ask your coach first.
Still stuck? Contact us and tell us the player name and what screen you were on.

coach.q: How do I get players onto my team?
coach.intro: Players join your team — you do not create their accounts for them.

steps.text: Send your players the team join link. They open it and confirm which player they are joining as.
Anyone waiting to be let on shows under New Player Onboard — approve them there.
Once they are on, they appear in the Roster.
If a player says the link does not work, check you still have an open spot on the team.

coach.q: How do I give a player full access?
coach.intro: Full access comes from a slot on your coach account — you hold the slots and apply them to players.

steps.text: Open Upgrade Players to see the slots you have and who is using them.
Apply a slot to a player and their account upgrades straight away.
Out of slots? Buy more from the same screen — they sit on your account until you use them.
A player joining a team with slots available is upgraded automatically, so you do not have to do it twice.

coach.intro: Homework is how you tell a player exactly what to train this week.

steps.text: Open the Coach’s Board.
Pick the folder or videos you want assigned.
Choose who gets it — the whole team, or just the players who need that skill.
Set a due date. Anything with a due date is what players see first.

coach.q: How do I see who has done their homework?
coach.intro: Everything a player marks done flows straight back to you.

steps.text: Open the Coach’s Board to see each player against what you assigned them.
For the written-up version, open the Homework Report.
To see one player in detail — every video, when they did it — open Player Detail.

coach.q: How do I chase a player who has fallen behind?
coach.intro: Nudge before you chase — most players just forgot.

steps.text: On the Coach’s Board, send a reminder to any player with overdue homework. You can send to one player or to everyone overdue at once.
Send a thumbs up to the players who did train. Recognition moves the group more than chasing does.
If a player has gone quiet for weeks, message them directly.

coach.q: How do I set a goal for the team?
coach.intro: A weekly goal gives every report something to measure against.

steps.text: Open Edit Team & Set Goals and set the weekly training target.
For individual targets, set them per player under Player Goals.
Review against the goal weekly in the Training Report.

coach.intro: Different challenges suit different problems — pick by what your team needs this week.

steps.text: Team gone quiet? Run the 24 to 48 Hour Challenge — short window, quick spike in training.
Want something running all month? Use the Team Contest or the Monthly Challenge.
Want players competing head to head? Point them at Challenge Teammates and the 1v1 boards.
Want a long, steady target? The Player Race runs the whole team toward one distance.

coach.q: Where does my team rank against other teams?
coach.intro: The team boards rank your whole club against everyone else on the platform.

steps.text: Team Leaderboard is the headline board — total team training.
Team Race ranks teams by distance covered.
Team Levels ranks teams by the levels their players have reached.
All three move off the same thing: players marking videos done.

coach.intro: Four reports, each answering a different question.

steps.text: Training Report — did the team train this week?
Homework Report — did they do what I assigned?
Player Detail — what exactly has this one player done?
Club Report — the shareable summary for parents and club staff.

coach.q: How do I get parents to see the progress?
coach.intro: Parents stay bought in when they can see the work — send them something they can open.

steps.text: Send the Club Report link — it opens outside the app, so parents do not need a login.
Post wins to Team Posts so the whole group sees who is training.
Point parents at their own player’s public profile for badges and totals.

coach.q: A player says something is not working — what do I check?
coach.intro: Work down this list before escalating; it is nearly always one of the first three.

steps.text: Check they are on the right team in the Roster, and that their account has full access.
If videos are locked, they need a slot applying.
If homework looks empty to them, confirm the assignment actually went to that player on the Coach’s Board.
Still stuck? Contact us with the team name, the player name and what screen they were on.

coach.intro: Yes — the Learning Center covers the same ground in short videos.

steps.text: Open the Learning Center.
Start with How to Get Started, then How to Use the All Programs Area.
These are worth sending to new players in their first week.
